airport.name: Capitán Av. German Quiroga G. Airport

summary: Capitán Av. German Quiroga G. Airport serves San Borja, a town in the Beni Department of Bolivia situated within the Amazon basin. As a small regional airport, it provides vital air access to a region known for ecotourism, wildlife, and indigenous communities. The facility primarily handles domestic flights connecting travelers to La Paz and other Bolivian hubs.
faqs:
Q: What is the main purpose of Capitán Av. German Quiroga G. Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves as a regional gateway for travelers visiting San Borja and the surrounding Beni region, supporting both tourism and local commerce in this part of the Bolivian Amazon.

Q: Are there international flights at this airport?
A: No, SRJ operates as a domestic airport, handling only flights within Bolivia.

Q: What is the airport named after?
A: It is named after Capitán Av. German Quiroga G., honoring a Bolivian aviation figure.

Q: How far is the airport from San Borja town center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from central San Borja, making ground transfers relatively quick and straightforward.
transport_tips: Taxis and mototaxis are typically available at the airport for the short ride into San Borja town. Arranging transport in advance with a local guide or hotel is recommended, especially during the rainy season when road conditions can be challenging. Flights into SRJ are sometimes affected by weather, so building flexibility into travel plans is wise.
local_tip: Carry small Boliviano bills, as change for larger denominations can be difficult to obtain from taxi drivers and small shops in this rural area of the Beni Department.
